stances_toward.note: Belgium aligned with Rabat on the Sahara: the Joint Declaration signed in Brussels on 23 Oct 2025 and Prevot's visit to Rabat (2 Mar 2026), where he called the autonomy plan the 'most credible basis' for a solution and announced economic steps in the southern provinces (trade missions, a consulate general in Rabat covering the whole territory). Belgium did not formally recognise Moroccan sovereignty in the sources found. Morocco was the top origin of new Belgian citizens in 2018 (13%, Statbel), which is why diaspora politics weigh on the file. Bond - affinity.

stances_toward.note: Transactional partnership since the 7 Apr 2022 joint declaration: Madrid backs the autonomy plan for Western Sahara (welcomed UNSCR 2797 on 4 Dec 2025 at the 13th High-Level Meeting), bilateral trade EUR 21bn in 2025, Albares speaks to Bourita 'daily'. But cooling after the July 2026 Ceuta crossing (about 49,000 entries by the Spanish count), Moroccan ministers' statements on Ceuta and Melilla in August 2026, and Spain's refusal to discuss sovereignty. Not rival: Madrid stresses cooperation and has not blamed Rabat. Bond - grievance: the standing Moroccan claim on Ceuta and Melilla, the 2021 Ghali crisis.

relations_to.summary: Ceuta crossing of 29-31 Jul 2026 - about 49,000 entries by the Spanish count (60,000 per Ceuta's mayor), more than 100 deaths reported, most people returned to Morocco within days. Sanchez called it an attack on territorial integrity but did not blame Rabat; Morocco denies orchestrating it and says smuggling networks used a misread Spanish Supreme Court ruling of 29 Jun on summary returns. Figures are provisional and conflict across outlets.
relations_to.note: Counts conflict: 49,000 (government), 60,000 (Ceuta's mayor), about 80,000 (Wikipedia lead); deaths 72 to 141 across dates. Wikipedia is used only as an index here; the primary reporting cited is CNN, NPR and Al Jazeera.
